_comment: The update manifest Hempdustry checks for itself, and the only place a new version has to be
announced. Read over https://raw.githubusercontent.com/, which is CDN-served and needs no API
key, no approval and no review queue -- so it reaches a player whichever site they got the mod
from. CurseForge and NexusMods both forbid embedding an API key in a distributed jar, so this
file is the only way those players can be told anything at all.
The shape is Forge's update-checker format on purpose, even though this is a Fabric mod: a
NeoForge build points `updateJSONURL` straight at this same file and needs no new work.
MAINTAINING IT: a key per Minecraft version. `-latest` is the newest build of any kind and is
what the in-game checker reads; `-recommended` is the newest *stable* one, and stays absent
until a stable exists. Both are read by NeoForge. Version strings are compared as semver with
build metadata ignored, so `2.0.0-beta+1.21.11` and `2.0.0-beta` compare equal -- the full jar
version is written here because it is what a player sees on the file they downloaded.
This file is hand-maintained, which is its one cost: bump it as part of cutting a release, or
the checker is confidently wrong, which is worse than silent. It is a step in release.md.
